summary: This note argues that sportsmanship is the cornerstone of amateur athletics, shaping character, community and resilience beyond the scores. It draws on quotes from coaches, players and a principal in local leagues and schools to show how respect, unity, mentorship and valuing the journey over results benefit participants and society.
one_line: Amateur athletics teach respect, unity, resilience and character through sportsmanship, illustrated by local coaches, players and a principal.
key_facts: Coach Michael Johnson coaches a youth soccer team at Jefferson Park and says winning is great but 'the way you play the game, the respect you show to your teammates and opponents, that's what you'll carry with you throughout life.'
Anita Rodriguez is captain of the 'Lightning Bolts,' a local adult softball team preparing for a championship game next Thursday.
Anita Rodriguez says her team wants to win but not at the cost of integrity or the fun of the game, and they applaud good play wherever they see it.
Jackson High School's flag football team, led by Coach Sarah Thompson, secured its division title last season, and the celebration spilled into the town.
Coach Sarah Thompson said the title was about the entire community coming together: 'That unity, that's the true win for us.'
Kevin Wallace, goalkeeper for 'The Crusaders' community league soccer team, allowed a critical goal that put the season at risk, and teammates reminded him they win and lose as a team.
Grace Lim, a volunteer coach for her daughter's track team, says 'The medals will gather dust, but the memories, the friendships, and the lessons will brighten their lives forever.'
Principal Gary Stevens spoke at Riverside Middle School's annual sports awards night, saying true character shows in how you carry yourself when no one is watching.
Jenny Martins, a veteran player in the town's volleyball league, has watched young players evolve into leaders and shy individuals become confident team players.
The note defines sportsmanship as respect for the rules, the officials, the opposition, and oneself.
Amateur teams often lack the resources of professional counterparts, yet adversity offers opportunities for growth and bonding.
The note concludes that amateur sports teams nurture the citizens of tomorrow, fostering fair play, respect and unity.
